heroTitle: Your model. Your data. Your rules.
heroDescription: The post-training stack in one CLI. Prepare your data, fine-tune your model, and know when it is ready to ship.
heroNote: Free and Apache-2.0 licensed. No account. No vendor lock-in.
workflowDescription: One connected workflow. Inspect each step to see what happens between your dataset and your next model.
descData: Check your dataset before spending GPU time. Find duplicates, formatting problems, and gaps in coverage.
descMethod: Work out whether you need prompting, RAG, supervised fine-tuning, or preference optimization.
descConfig: Start with a recipe. Keep the model, data, and training settings in one readable YAML file.
descTrain: Train on your own hardware. Use LoRA and optional layer streaming when GPU memory is limited.
descEval: Evaluate the task and check for regressions. Keep the evidence next to the model you produced.
descExport: Export your model and connect it to the serving tools you already use.
dataTitle: Good training starts before the first token.
dataDescription: Your documents, conversations, and examples become the foundation of your model. Inspect the data, remove duplicates, and understand what you are teaching it.
dataFeature1: Dataset checks before the GPU run
dataFeature3: Your files stay under your control
evalTitle: A falling loss is only the beginning.
evalDescription: Evaluate what your model learned, catch regressions, and make the release decision explicit. Soup brings the training loop and its evidence together.
evalFeature3: A clear SHIP or DON'T SHIP verdict
streamTitle: Make the model fit your hardware.
streamDescription: Optional layer streaming moves frozen weights from RAM or NVMe into GPU memory one layer at a time. Combine it with 4-bit quantization when supported.
streamNote: Layer streaming is BETA. Published measurements include the hardware, version, and limitations; throughput varies with your setup.
migrationDescription: Convert an existing configuration from LLaMA-Factory, Axolotl, or Unsloth. Review the generated YAML, check your data paths, then train.
ecosystemDescription: Train, track, export, and serve with the tools your ML workflow already depends on.
zeroDescription: A desktop workbench for the full AI workflow. Built on Soup. Coming soon.
finalDescription: Install Soup. Bring your data. Make something yours.
footerDescription: The open-source post-training stack. Built for people who build models.
footerLicense: Apache-2.0 licensed. An open-source project by MePlay, Inc.
animationData: Animated cloud of documents representing a training dataset
ornament: Kazakh qoshqar muyiz ornament drawn in ASCII
aboutTitle: A complete workshop for your next model.
aboutDescription: Training a useful model takes more than a training loop. Your data needs checking. Your method needs choosing. Your configuration needs to fit the hardware. And your results need evidence. Soup brings those jobs into one open-source CLI, from the first dataset to the final release.
aboutNote: Your hardware, your files, your configuration. Keep every part of the workflow inspectable and make it your own.
installTitle: Three commands. A place to start.
installDescription: Install the training package, create your first configuration, then start a run. Review the generated settings and point the configuration at your own data.
methodsDescription: Supervised fine-tuning, preference optimization, reinforcement learning, and distillation. Start with the method your task needs and keep the rest of your workflow familiar.
dataDeepTitle: Understand the data before you train on it.
dataDeepDescription: Inspect formats, remove semantic duplicates, map topic coverage, and check for memorized secrets. Turn exported production traces into training examples and preference pairs.
trainDeepTitle: From one laptop to a distributed run.
trainDeepDescription: Use LoRA or QLoRA, pick the layers worth training, or scale out with DeepSpeed and FSDP. Apple Silicon has a native MLX path. Layer streaming is an opt-in BETA for models that do not fit in GPU memory.
shipDeepDescription: Derive an evaluation suite from your data, lock its definition, and check task quality alongside general capability. Keep the release verdict and its evidence beside the weights.
operateTitle: Keep understanding your model after training.
operateDescription: Diagnose failure modes, investigate a loss spike, compare adapters, and bisect a regression. Manage the adapter lifecycle with diff, merge, checks, and a lockfile for the base model, dataset, and environment.
secureTitle: A workflow your team can inspect.
secureDescription: Generate model bills of materials and signed provenance, enforce release gates in CI, and start from governance-oriented configuration templates. Connect your coding agent through Soup's MCP server with explicit execution controls.
recipesTitle: A recipe for the work in front of you.
recipesDescription: Start with a concrete configuration for your model and task. Inspect it, change it, and keep it in version control. Soup recipes cover text, preference training, vision, and audio workflows.
modelsTitle: Bring the models you already work with.
modelsDescription: Work with the Hugging Face ecosystem and model families including Llama, Qwen, Gemma, Mistral, Phi, DeepSeek, and Whisper. Method, architecture, and backend support vary; check the documentation for your run.
communityTitle: Built in the open. Better together.
communityDescription: Read the source, reproduce a measurement, report a problem, or share what worked on your hardware. Contributions and real-world results help Soup improve.
faq1q: Do I need a large GPU?
faq1a: Requirements depend on the model, sequence length, method, and batch size. LoRA and quantization reduce memory needs. Optional layer streaming can help with larger models, with BETA limitations and a speed tradeoff.
faq2q: Can I use an existing training configuration?
faq2a: Soup can migrate configurations from LLaMA-Factory, Axolotl, and Unsloth. Review the generated YAML and resolve your actual dataset paths before starting the run.
faq3q: Does Soup upload my training data?
faq3a: Local workflows operate on your own files and hardware. Cloud execution, remote models, tracking integrations, and publishing are separate choices that you configure.
faq4a: Soup CLI is available now as an Apache-2.0 open-source package. Soup Zero, the desktop workbench, is coming soon. Follow the documentation for the current release's supported features.
themeHint: Choose a theme. Arrow keys to browse, Enter to apply, Escape to close.
ecosysTraceTitle: Your production traces are training data.
ecosysTraceDescription: Bring exports from the observability tools you already use. Soup normalizes the traces into a local JSONL stream for your data workflow.
ecosysTraceNote: The export path runs offline. Langfuse also supports a live pull; other providers use an exported file.
ecosysHuggingface: Pull models and publish to the Hub
ecosysGguf: Dynamic, IQ and ARM quantization targets
ecosysHqq: HQQ, AQLM and more quantization formats
ecosysSupportNote: Choose the integration your run needs. Backend, architecture, hardware and optional package requirements vary.
zeroPageStatus: Workbench coming soon. CLI available now.
zeroPageHeroBody: A desktop workspace for the entire model lifecycle. Explore, adapt, evaluate and serve open models with your own data and compute.
zeroPageHeroNote: Open source. Your infrastructure. No account required for the CLI.
zeroPagePreviewNote: This is a workbench concept, not a running training job. Training, evaluation and serving are available today through the Soup CLI.
zeroPageWhyTitle: Your model work has outgrown the tabs.
zeroPageWhyBody: A workbench should connect the experiments, the data and the decision to ship.
zeroPagePainSimpleBody: Simple interfaces reach their limit when the task needs real post-training.
zeroPagePainComplexBody: Scripts, notebooks and dashboards scatter the evidence from every run.
zeroPagePainPrivateBody: Sensitive datasets and adapted weights belong on infrastructure you control.
zeroPageGraphLabel: Documents and experiment fragments assemble into a connected graph as you scroll.
zeroPageGraphNote: One place for the context behind your next model.
zeroPageStationsTitle: From the first prompt to production.
zeroPageStationsBody: The desktop workbench is in development. Three stations already have a working engine in the open-source CLI.
zeroPageStationPlaygroundBody: Explore open models before changing them.
zeroPageStationDataBody: Prepare, clean and label the material your model learns from.
zeroPageStationPromptsBody: Develop instructions and compare their behaviour.
zeroPageStationRagBody: Bring relevant documents into the conversation.
zeroPageStationAgentsBody: Connect model actions and MCP tools.
zeroPageStationTrainBody: Adapt model weights to your own examples.
zeroPageStationEvalsBody: Check task quality and regressions before release.
zeroPageStationDeployBody: Serve a model on compute you control.
zeroPageOwnershipTitle: Your hardware. Your data. Your model.
zeroPageOwnershipBody: Work locally or on cloud GPUs you control. The workbench is being built around the live training, evaluation and serving engine; model work does not pass through Soup infrastructure.
zeroPageWaysBody: Choose the amount of control a task needs. The visual and copilot interfaces are planned; the terminal path works today.
zeroPageNoCodeBody: Choose a model, dataset and recipe. Let the workbench prepare the settings.
zeroPageCopilotBody: Describe the outcome. The copilot coordinates the stations.
zeroPageCodeBody: Keep full control of reproducible commands and configuration.
zeroPageCopilotRequest: Adapt Llama to our support tickets, then check whether it is ready for release.
zeroPageCopilotReply: Plan: prepare the dataset, fine-tune, evaluate. Keep the release verdict and its evidence together.
zeroPageCopilotPlaceholder: Ask about a training, evaluation or deployment task…
zeroPageConceptOnly: Interface concept · not connected to a model
zeroPageGateNote: A release decision needs task improvement, preserved general ability and checks against metric gaming.
zeroPageWorkflowTitle: Raw data in. A model you can stand behind out.
zeroPageWorkflowBody: Explore, prepare, train, evaluate and deploy. Production feedback becomes the next dataset.
zeroPageVerdictBody: A run produces a SHIP or DON'T SHIP decision with an evidence file your team can commit, inspect and re-check.
zeroPageVerdictExample: Example verdict, not a measured result
zeroPageCtaBody: Install the open-source CLI for fine-tuning, evaluation and serving. The desktop workbench is the next layer.
zeroPageAnimationLabel: A rotating field of ASCII characters connects into a model workspace.
hirePageHeroBody: I build fast, accessible interfaces with AI in the loop from the first sketch to production, and I can take on the backend too.
hirePageSkillsTitle: What I bring to a team.
hirePageSkillsBody: Frontend is the core. AI is how I work. The backend is there when the product needs one person to own the whole feature.
hirePageFrontendBody: Interfaces from design to production: components, motion, responsive layout, accessibility and performance.
hirePageBackendBody: APIs, data and deployment, so a feature can ship end to end without waiting on another team.
hirePageAiBody: AI agents are part of my daily workflow. They make me faster; tests, reviews and verification keep the quality bar.
hirePageProofBody: The Soup landing page you are reading: a static multilingual site with a documentation reader and checks that run on every build.
hirePageCtaBody: Tell me about the role or the project. Write to me on Telegram.
hirePageExpBody: Products I have built and teams I work with, from healthcare software to my own app with real users.
